metric: deceleration the assumed service brake can hold against gravity
target: holds on a 25 % slope: brake deceleration >= g * sin(atan 0.25) = 2.38 m/s2
measured: assumed dry braking 2.50 m/s2 against 2.38 needed
note: margin 5 %. The winter planning value (1.50 m/s2) is the available friction on a slippery surface, not the brake's capacity, so it is not compared here. The brake itself has to be measured on the machine.

metric: stopping distance from the standard's test speed (top speed when below 32 km/h)
target: below the table limit; the limit formula must be read from the purchased standard
measured: twin stops from 19.8 km/h in 7.8 m
note: The limit formula is unreadable in the free sample. A commonly quoted form (v2/150 + 0.2(v + 5), v in km/h) would give 7.6 m, which the twin's assumed braking would miss. Confirm the formula in the purchased standard, then measure the real brake.

source: ISO 13855 (approach speed of a walking person)
metric: highest walking speed the adversarial search and the shifts use
measured: adversarial walker speeds up to 2.0 m/s
note: The fields are sized for the machine's stopping distance, as ISO 3691-4 does; a person walking into a machine that has already stopped is outside the stop function.

metric: a standing test piece (200 mm diameter) just inside the far edge of each protective field
target: detected in every field set, on the axis and at both far corners
note: Missed at 1 degree resolution: fwd_3.0_S/front at (8.82, 1.89); fwd_3.0_S/front at (8.82, -1.89). The fields are measured from the bucket's front edge, but the scanners sit about 3 m behind it: the far edge is up to 8.1 m from the nearest scanner, beyond the 4 m protective range the speed cap assumes. The twin's scanners see 15 m, so the shifts never showed it. The full machine needs a rated sensor with that range (or one mounted further forward), or a lower speed cap.

metric: scan plane height against the lying test piece
target: scan plane at or below 70 mm, or another means of detecting a person lying down
measured: scan plane 0.5 m on the full machine, about 0.085 m on the 1:8 testbed
note: A horizontal scan plane at 0.5 m passes over a 70 mm lying test piece, so a person lying on the ground is not detected by the safety scanners. ISO 3691-4 is written for indoor trucks with low scanners. Options: a second, low scan plane; a rated 3D sensor; or stating it as a residual risk covered by site access control. Not yet decided in the safety concept.

metric: rated operating load against the full-turn static tipping load and a bucket of sand
target: rated load = 50 % of the tipping load and >= the struck bucket of sand
measured: rated load 9.1 kg, tipping load 18.21 kg, bucket of sand 8.2 kg
note: From CAD mass properties; weigh the built machine to confirm.

metric: PL of the stop function from component data
target: PL d calculated from the selected components' MTTFd, DC and CCF
note: Needs MTTFd, DC and CCF from the data sheets of the selected safety relay, relays and scanners (SISTEMA or hand calculation).

source: Dadhich et al. 2019, Volvo L180H field test (expert fills in 6-8 s; automatic 26 % longer)
metric: mean fill time and fill factor of the learned policy on the held-out test episodes
target: fill time <= 1.26 x 7 s = 8.8 s and fill factor >= 0.90
measured: fill time 8.7 s, fill factor 0.94 (200 held-out episodes)
note: Simulated bucket-pile model against a field result on a larger machine (L180H); it shows the policy is in the published range, not that the model is right.

source: Aoshima & Servin 2024, WA320-7: simulation differs from the machine by about 11 % in force
metric: learned policy on gravel with digging resistance 11 % lower and 11 % higher
target: fill factor >= 0.85 and every episode completes in both cases
measured: resistance x0.89: fill 1.03, 9.2 s, success 100 %; resistance x1.00: fill 1.02, 9.6 s, success 100 %; resistance x1.11: fill 1.00, 9.8 s, success 100 %
note: Covers the published sim-to-real force error as a change in digging resistance only.

source: Frank et al. 2012, 73 operators on a Volvo loader, short loading cycle
metric: KAUHA cycle time against the measured novice-to-professional spread
target: reported against the spread; the paper gives it only in plots
measured: KAUHA median cycle 69 s (truck loading, twin)
note: The operator study reports cycle times only in plots. Needs the figures digitised or the pilot site's own operator timing.

source: Tampere University, 6 t wheel loader short Y-cycle recording (CC BY 4.0)
metric: twin driven with the recorded operator inputs: cylinder trajectories and phase durations
note: The recording's channel list is in its documentation PDF, which could not be read from the build environment. The replay will be written against that list, not guessed.

source: attack classes of the ROAD CAN dataset: fabrication, fuzzing, replay, masquerade, suspension
metric: attack frames accepted by the gateway or the PLC, and unsafe commands that follow
target: 0 forged frames accepted; replay and suspension end in a stop within the frame timeout
measured: fuzzing: 82 of 200000 random frames accepted (0.041 %); replay: 12.5 % accepted; masquerade with a computed CRC: gateway released in 400 of 400 cycles while the PLC said stop; suspension: brake after 0.105 s
note: The CRC and alive counter detect faults, not attackers: they use no secret, so anyone on the bus can forge frames. The stop itself survives (the PLC cuts power through relays, not over CAN), but a forged RemoteHeartbeat could hide a lost link or a pressed remote e-stop. The bus needs message authentication (for example AUTOSAR SecOC with a CMAC) or physical separation of the safety segment before it leaves a closed test area. Suspension is handled.

metric: real vehicle traffic replayed onto the KAUHA bus, as recorded and remapped onto KAUHA identifiers
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_ROAD to a folder of candump logs.

metric: person recall and precision at confidence 0.25
target: recall >= 0.80, precision >= 0.75 (the values measured on Construction-PPE)
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_SODA to a YOLO-layout copy (images/, labels/).

metric: frames with a protective field occupied although no labelled object is inside it
target: false-occupied rate reported per sensor; target below 1 % of frames after the dust filter
note: Set KAUHA_DATA_LIDARDUSTX to the dataset folder (research-use licence).

metric: false-occupied rate and missed people in snow against dry runs
note: Needs the dataset's calibration and label format in hand before a loader is written.

source: RADIATE; 4D radar in an open-pit mine
metric: radar detections of people when lidar is degraded
note: Radar replay needs the radar's role fixed first (detection only, or part of a field).

metric: position error and time to declare the position invalid
note: Needs the benchmark's file format and the EKF run from logged GNSS/IMU instead of the twin.
